description: Migrate worker dispatch from forbidden claude -p headless mode to interactive TUI + sentinel polling, deleting the exit/wait-for path entirely.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: claude "query" opens an interactive session with an initial prompt; --agent selects the session agent; --session-id accepts a UUID; --permission-mode works in interactive mode; -p/--print is the SDK headless mode and is forbidden in this project. claude --bg / claude agents --json (background sessions) exists as a future alternative to the tmux pane model: out of scope here.

userStories.title: Wire sentinel mode as the only implementer dispatch in cam next
userStories.description: As the cam orchestrator, I need cam next to spawn the implementer worker as an interactive TUI claude session and poll a sentinel for completion, so that no claude -p headless invocation is ever issued (subscription rule).
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/next.ts no longer hardcodes implementerMode 'exit'; the implementer is dispatched via the existing sentinel branch using buildImplementerWorkerArgv({ interactive: true }).

The implementer claude is launched as `claude --permission-mode <mode> --session-id <uuid> --agent subagent-implementer '<taskPrompt>'` with no -p, no --output-format, and no '; tmux wait-for -S' chain.
Session UUIDs passed via --session-id are generated with crypto.randomUUID() (lowercase) so the transcript filename resolves correctly.
No new config knob is introduced in project.toml or CLI flags; sentinel is the single default path.
test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts still passes (no --permission-mode on cam subcommands; it is forwarded only to the spawned claude).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/next.ts (around lines 498, 564, 747 where mode 'exit' is hardcoded and the 'sentinel mode is not wired in production today' comment lives), src/supervisor/worker-argv.ts (buildImplementerWorkerArgv interactive branch already exists from US-012 of CAM-22), src/supervisor/loop.ts (sentinel branch). Sentinel is corroboration only: handoff+prd remain primary signals (CAM-32 lesson: state-primary). UUIDs must be lowercase on macOS (uuidgen quirk, see memory). Keep the implementer worker invocation shape identical to the scaffold tested in test/supervisor/.

userStories.title: Harden pane capture for TUI by reading full scrollback
userStories.description: As the supervisor poller, I need capture-pane to read the full pane history so the sentinel line is detected even after the TUI scrolls it off the visible region, and the prompt echo cannot be mistaken for a sentinel.
acceptanceCriteria: Both capturePane adapter call sites in src/commands/next.ts (around lines 498 and 564) invoke `tmux capture-pane -p -S -` (full history), not the default visible-only capture.

A regression test feeds the literal initial taskPrompt text (which mentions 'CAM_IMPLEMENTER_STATUS=' without a story= field) into parseAnySentinel and asserts the result is null, proving the TUI prompt echo cannot trigger a false sentinel hit.
Existing supervisor tests under test/supervisor/ continue to pass without modification of sentinel semantics.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/next.ts (two capturePane adapters near lines 498 and 564), src/supervisor/sentinel.ts (parseAnySentinel is the assertion target), test/supervisor/ (new fixture asserting prompt-echo non-match). CAM-35 lesson: sentinel parse is a recurrent fragility class, so add the fixture with the exact prompt string used by US-001's implementer dispatch.

userStories.title: Interactive reviewer dispatch with prompt and sentinel polling
userStories.description: As the supervisor review step, I need the reviewer claude to run as an interactive TUI with an explicit task prompt and permission-mode, and completion detected by polling for the <review> verdict tag, so the review path actually works headless-free (CAM-41 fix).
acceptanceCriteria: src/supervisor/review.ts exposes an interactive variant of buildReviewerWorkerArgv that accepts taskPrompt and permissionMode (mirroring buildImplementerWorkerArgv) and emits no -p flag, no --output-format, and no wait-for chain.
The reviewer task prompt is: "Review all changes on the current branch vs main per your AGENT.md. Run the project quality gates. End your output with the <review> verdict tag on the very last line."

makeReviewDispatch polls capture-pane for the <review> tag, with the same pane-died and timeout handling as the implementer sentinel branch in src/supervisor/loop.ts, instead of relying on a tmux wait-for channel.
Unit tests assert the interactive reviewer argv contains '--agent', '--session-id', '--permission-mode', and the taskPrompt, and does NOT contain '-p' or 'wait-for'.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/review.ts (buildReviewerWorkerArgv + makeReviewDispatch), src/supervisor/loop.ts (sentinel branch is the polling reference), test/supervisor/review.test.ts (or equivalent). CAM-41 root cause: the -p reviewer path passed neither prompt nor permission-mode, so the review never worked headless. The poll target is the literal '<review>' tag, distinct from CAM_*_STATUS sentinels.

userStories.title: Delete the exit/wait-for dispatch path end to end
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need every trace of the headless exit + tmux wait-for machinery removed so there is exactly one dispatch model (interactive TUI + sentinel polling), preventing accidental regression to claude -p.
acceptanceCriteria: src/supervisor/worker-argv.ts and src/supervisor/review.ts no longer emit `; tmux -L cam wait-for -S <channel>` chains in any code path.
The `channel` parameter is removed from argv builders and from any options where it becomes dead.
waitFor wiring is removed from src/commands/next.ts and from the options of runSupervisor and makeReviewDispatch.
The 'exit' branch in src/supervisor/loop.ts is removed; implementerMode is simplified to a single sentinel path (or the `mode` concept is removed entirely if no longer needed).
Tests assert ABSENCE of '-p' and 'wait-for' substrings in the shell strings produced by both implementer and reviewer argv builders.
Existing loop/review tests that injected a waitFor stub are updated to the new sentinel-only contract.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/worker-argv.ts, src/supervisor/review.ts, src/supervisor/loop.ts, src/commands/next.ts, test/supervisor/*.test.ts. This is a deletion-only story; do not deprecate, do not leave a feature flag. Watch for callers of waitFor across the supervisor module graph. Keep MIT headers in src/retry/* untouched (none of these files are ported retry code, but verify before deleting adjacent shared helpers).

userStories.title: Operator validation: full loop with TUI workers, no claude -p process
userStories.description: As the operator, I need to run a complete cam plan + cam next cycle against a real test issue and confirm via process inspection that no `claude -p` process is ever spawned, the TUI workers reach sentinel and idle without consuming tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: A test issue is processed end to end with `bun index.ts plan` followed by `bun index.ts next`, producing an implemented story and a recorded review verdict, both via TUI workers.
During the run, `ps aux | grep claude` is inspected (multiple samples) and shows zero processes whose argv contains `-p` or `--print`.
Post-sentinel, the implementer pane idle is confirmed not to consume tokens: the session transcript file mtime stops advancing after the sentinel line is emitted.
Operator captures evidence (screencap of ps output and transcript mtime delta) and attaches it to the PR or issue thread.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Requires a real subscription claude session, a tmux server, and the operator's machine. The session transcript lives at the path derived from --session-id (lowercase UUID on macOS); use the project's known transcript path helper to read mtime. Do NOT run this against a stale PATH binary (see memory); use `bun index.ts` from the branch. CAM-39/40/41 are absorbed by this validation: confirm they no longer reproduce.
